Today's focus was on defining new protocol specifications for post-execution transactions and Sequencer-Defined Metering (SDM) within the Optimism ecosystem. Several issues related to testing, sync, and transaction pool behavior were also addressed and closed.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Protocol Specification Updates
- **Post-Execution Transaction and SDM Specs Defined:** New specifications were added for the `0x7D` Post-Execution Transaction envelope and version-1 Sequencer-Defined Metering (SDM) payload schema. This work involved updates to the glossary and various protocol overview documents, particularly within the `specs/protocol` directory. ([#908](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/908))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Testing and CI Improvements
- **Flaky Fuzz Test Addressed:** An intermittent "Too long with no output" failure in the `op-e2e-fuzz` CircleCI job was investigated. The root cause was identified as excessive CPU usage during binary startup due to a full genesis pipeline run for all alloc types and hardfork modes. A fix is underway to lazily generate alloc types, significantly reducing startup time and preventing future timeouts. ([#21191](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21191))
- **`op-up` Test Removal:** The `op-up` test (`TestRun`) was removed from consideration for CI integration as the `op-up` package itself was deleted. ([#21202](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21202))
- **Misfiled Flaky Test Report:** A report for a flaky `TestL2OutputSubmitter/honest` test was closed as it was determined to be filed in error, originating from a spurious cross-pipeline signal rather than an actual failure in the relevant PR's CI. ([#21231](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21231))

### Sync and Metrics Issues
- **Sequencer Sync Stability:** An issue where the follow-mode sequencer's `latestHead` failed to re-anchor past a `FollowSource` `forceReset` under EL-sync was closed. After extensive testing, the flake could not be reproduced, suggesting the issue was related to how a previous invalid message replacement test was written. ([#21125](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21125))
- **`op-supernode` Sync Test Integration:** The issue regarding integrating `op-supernode` with `op-sync-tester` and adding an extended nightly sync test was partially addressed and closed. The decision was made to skip further integration as longer-running tests should not rely on `sync-tester` due to its EL mocking. ([#21096](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21096))
- **Kona Metrics Cardinality:** A bug causing very high cardinality for exported metrics in Kona was fixed. ([#19927](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19927))

### Transaction Pool Behavior
- **Interop Tx Pool Failsafe:** An issue where `op-reth`'s transaction pool failed to resume accepting interop transactions after the failsafe was disabled (requiring a restart) was resolved. The fix involves restarting both `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder` on affected sequencers. A gauge metric is proposed to make the failsafe state observable. ([#21149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21149))

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were opened today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### `op-reth-test-engine` Development
- **Minimal In-Test EL for `op-e2e/actions`:** Progress is being made on creating a minimal in-test Execution Layer (EL) for `op-e2e/actions` and achieving Rust action-test parity. The implementation is underway as a stacked series of PRs. The first PR focuses on establishing the `op-reth-test-engine` foundation with an `EphemeralChain` and `TestEngine` wrapper. The approach reuses the real `op-reth` stack for storage, validation, and block building, avoiding reimplementation. Future PRs will cover one-shot block execution, stateful in-flight payload building, lib API finalization, and OP-semantics golden-vector tests. ([#20415](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20415))

# ethereum-optimism/specs Daily Update (Jun 5, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
The day saw significant progress in addressing critical issues related to interop network stability and synchronization, with a focus on resolving EL sync recovery stalls and devstack configuration.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Devstack Interop Configuration Fixed
A configuration issue in the devstack interop preset, where the same Execution Layer (EL) was incorrectly shared between the supernode and the light node sequencer, has been resolved. This fix improves the isolation and stability of devstack environments. [#21158](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21158)

### Interop Reorg Recovery Decision
The issue concerning `op-conductor`'s graceful recovery from interop reorgs has been closed. The decision was made not to implement automatic recovery, opting instead for manual intervention and the development of runbooks to handle such situations. [#20006](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/20006)

## NEW ISSUES

### Interop Specs Reclassification
A new issue has been opened to move interop specifications from the "experimental" section to "lagoon." This reclassification aims to clarify that the hardfork part of interop will activate alongside other features like SDM. [#915](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/915)

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### op-supernode/op-reth: CL sync recovery can stall when SafeDB/bookkeeping references EL-missing block [#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21076)
The discussion on this issue continues to focus on identifying the root cause of CL sync recovery stalls. Recent updates indicate that a candidate fix from reth ([paradigmxyz/reth#24875](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/24875)) did not resolve the wedge, and in some cases, reproduced the issue more reliably. The problem appears to stem from a cyclic deadlock in reth's `StateTrieOverlayManager` / `DeferredTrieData` machinery, specifically due to locks being held across `rayon` computes. Two distinct sites for this anti-pattern have been identified, and two patches (eager and lazy + sequential sort) have been developed and are being tested. Initial soak tests with these patches show promising results, with continuous CL-sync for several hours without wedges. The issue is being flagged for the reth team as it involves reth's `chain-state` code.

### op-supervisor/op-supernode cross-safe cannot drain a backlog faster than real-time after a stall [#21117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/21117)
The latest comment suggests that the observed 12.06-hour window for the cross-safe head to catch up after a multi-hour interruption is consistent with sequencer window expiry behavior. If the local safe head did indeed catch up to unsafe, and the sequencer window expired, manual intervention would be required. The current understanding is that if this behavior is expected, no further action is needed on this ticket.

### `opgeth-decoupling`: Migrating Tests and L2 Client
Discussions on [#20265](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20265) and [#20264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20264) highlight critical considerations for migrating integration tests and making `op-service/sources` the OP-aware Ethereum client. Key points include:
- **Receipt Index Correlation:** Tests that correlate `txs[i]` with `receipts[i]` by position will break when migrating to `InfoAndUserTxs` due to the exclusion of synthetic transactions. These tests must filter receipts in lockstep or use paired accessors.
- **Lagoon's `0x7D` Post-Exec Tx:** The Lagoon hardfork introduces a trailing `0x7D` post-execution transaction to L2 blocks. Tests assuming the only synthetic transaction is the leading `0x7E` deposit need to be updated to handle both.
- **L2 Transaction Representation:** A design resolution proposes partitioning L2 transaction accessors by transaction class instead of using an `optypes.Transaction` wrapper. This involves adding `InfoAndUserTxs`, `InfoAndDeposits`, and `InfoAndFirstDeposit` to `apis.EthClient` to handle different transaction types.
- **`0x7D` Routing:** Lagoon makes `0x7D` routing load-bearing, as the post-exec tx is a canonical block transaction. Accessors must route both `0x7E` and `0x7D` out for upstream go-ethereum compatibility.

### `opgeth-decoupling`: `op-core/types` and Call-Site Swaps
Discussions on [#20262](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20262) and [#20263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/20263) focus on creating `op-core/types` and swapping call-sites across various Optimism services. Key points include:
- **Transition-Only Helpers:** Helper functions like `IsDepositTx` and `SourceHash` that operate on `*types.Transaction` are considered transition scaffolding. They will be deleted after the final cutover to upstream go-ethereum, as upstream `*types.Transaction` cannot hold deposit or post-exec transactions.
- **Durable Shape:** The long-term approach is for callers to decode raw bytes into `optypes.DepositTx` or `optypes.PostExecTx` and read fields directly from the struct.
- **`PostExecTx` as Canonical:** The `PostExecTx` is a canonical block transaction in the Lagoon hardfork, participating in the L2 block transaction list. This reinforces the need for the decode path to handle both `0x7E` and `0x7D` transactions.
- **Call-Site Swap Strategy:** When swapping call sites, prioritize decoding to `optypes.DepositTx` via `UnmarshalDepositTx` and reading struct fields directly, rather than relying on the `*types.Transaction` helpers, if the raw transaction bytes are readily available.

Issue [#18323](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/18323) was closed as a duplicate of another issue. The original intent was to monitor ZK games and report on output agreement, expected root claim, and forecasted results, which would require significant refactoring to separate ZK-specific properties from generic ones.

- **No `optypes.Transaction` wrapper:** Instead of a wrapper, L2 transaction accessors will be partitioned by transaction class.
- **New `apis.EthClient` methods:** `InfoAndUserTxs` (excludes synthetic OP types), `InfoAndDeposits` (deposits as op-core structs), and `InfoAndFirstDeposit` (header + first tx) will be added.
- **Lagoon's `0x7D` routing:** The `0x7D` PostExecTx in Lagoon+ blocks is a canonical block transaction and must be routed out by accessors, similar to `0x7E` deposits.

For [#20262](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20262) (opgeth-decoupling: create op-core/types), a design note clarified:
- **Transition-only helpers:** `*types.Transaction` helpers like `IsDepositTx` are temporary and will be deleted after the final cutover to upstream go-ethereum, as upstream `*types.Transaction` cannot hold deposit or post-exec transactions.
- **`PostExecTx` as canonical block transaction:** In Lagoon, `PostExecTx` is a canonical block transaction, participating in the L2 block tx list, which necessitates its handling in the decode path.

Regarding [#20263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20263) (opgeth-decoupling: swap call-sites to op-core/*), it was noted that:
- **`optypes` helpers are transition scaffolding:** The `optypes` helpers are temporary and designed to allow call sites to drop dependency on op-geth's `Transaction` methods before the L2 transaction representation changes. They are not meant for building new long-lived APIs.
- **Prefer direct decoding:** Where possible, direct decoding to `optypes.DepositTx` via `UnmarshalDepositTx` is preferred over routing through `*types.Transaction` helpers.

This week’s activity centered on refining the protocol's Zero-Knowledge (ZK) infrastructure and clarifying execution specifications for the Lagoon SDM. The team focused on technical precision within the Lagoon SDM specification to ensure consistent execution behavior across the network.
*   **Lagoon SDM Warming Clarification:** A critical update was made to the Lagoon SDM specification regarding block-level warming. The clarification specifies that block-level warming excludes intrinsically-warm accesses. This ensures that only state accesses charged the EIP-2929 "cold" price are eligible for rebates, maintaining the economic integrity of the gas model ([#919](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/919)).

### ZK Infrastructure & Execution
Discussions continued regarding the technical requirements for supporting ZK execution within the protocol's tooling.
*   **VM-Runner ZK Support:** Technical scoping for `vm-runner` indicates that ZK execution will likely require a Rust-based implementation due to dependencies on `sp1`. Current proposals include embedding a Rust executor within a Docker image or adding a specific option to `vm-runner` to drive the executor while minimizing new code by leveraging existing proposer components ([#18325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18325)).

Several issues were closed this week as the project moved from specification/decision phases to active implementation in other repositories:

Collaboration focused on determining the boundaries between the protocol specifications and the practical implementation of ZK components. The decision to move several tracking issues to external repositories suggests a shift toward active development and integration testing within the broader Optimism ecosystem. - **Investigation into Flaky Blob Encoding Test**
  A detailed comment was added to [#21539](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21539) regarding the "Flaky test: FuzzDetectNonBijectivity mutates a non-encoded bit (op-service/eth)". The comment clarifies that the test's premise is incorrect because the blob code is not bijective on the top two bits of the first field element. Both `op-node` and `kona` implementations treat the first element differently, masking out the top two bits regardless of their setting, leading to the same decoded data even if these bits are flipped. This behavior means the test fails because no error is returned, and the data is decoded unchanged. The comment also discusses the implications of changing this behavior (potential for breaking existing on-chain blobs) and suggests that a fix might require a hardfork or an understanding that honest batchers would not post malformed blobs.

# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Weekly Report (Jun 21 - 27, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week’s activity focused on refining core protocol specifications and addressing technical debt within the Optimism stack's data handling layers. A significant technical investigation into blob encoding non-bijectivity highlighted potential discrepancies between `op-node` and `kona` implementations, sparking a critical discussion on data integrity and hardfork requirements. Additionally, new design documentation was introduced to address Post-Execution transactions within the Fault Proof / State Transition framework.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Fault Proof & State Transition Enhancements
The project continues to evolve its state transition and fault monitoring architectures.
*   **FMA: SDM / PostExec tx ([#388](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/388)):** A new pull request was opened to document the design for Post-Execution transactions within the State Deposit Model (SDM). This work is essential for ensuring the integrity of the state transition function after transaction execution.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### New & Active Issues
*   **Blob Encoding Non-Bijectivity ([#21539](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21539)):** A deep-dive investigation into a flaky test in `op-service/eth` revealed a fundamental characteristic of the current blob encoding implementation. The analysis found that the top two bits of the first field element are masked out by both `op-node` and `kona`, meaning the encoding is not bijective. This allows different encoded inputs to result in the same decoded data.
    *   **Impact:** The discussion highlights a potential risk where changing this behavior to enforce strict bijectivity could invalidate existing on-chain blobs. 
    *   **Proposed Path:** Resolution may require a protocol hardfork or a formal acceptance that honest batchers will naturally avoid malformed blob construction.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Technical collaboration this week was centered on cross-implementation consistency. The detailed analysis of the blob encoding issue demonstrates active coordination between developers working on the Go-based `op-node` and the Rust-based `kona` implementations. This level of scrutiny ensures that the Superchain maintains a unified state transition logic across different client software, which is vital for the security of the optimistic rollup mechanism.

In July 2026, development focused heavily on hardening the Superchain infrastructure through rigorous security audits and the refinement of deployment tooling. Significant progress was made on the `op-deployer` and `op-reth` components, alongside critical compatibility fixes for `op-node` regarding EIP-4444. The month was characterized by a transition toward production readiness for the SuperZKDG (Zero-Knowledge Data Generation) and Isthmus-related features, supported by comprehensive quality assurance reviews and security feedback integration from external auditors.

Significant enhancements were made to `op-deployer` to streamline chain launches and improve state management.

*   **Developer Experience:** A new tutorial was added to assist developers in deploying contracts to the OP Sepolia testnet ([#21607](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21607)).

### Protocol Security & SuperZKDG
The project prioritized the security of the SuperZKDG components in preparation for upcoming audits.
*   **Super ZK Game:** A fix was proposed to address quality assurance issues identified during internal reviews of the Super ZK game ([#21615](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21615)).
*   **Audit Integration:** Feedback from Lumi Security was actively integrated into the codebase, specifically targeting `lib.rs`, `l2_el.go`, `solutil.go`, and `kona` ([#21604](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21604), [#21606](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21606), [#21612](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21612), [#21613](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21613)).

### Node Performance & Compatibility
Refinements to `op-reth` and `op-node` addressed both network compatibility and transaction pool logic.
*   **EIP-4444 Compatibility:** A long-standing issue was resolved where `op-node` failed to determine the L2 genesis blockhash when L1 nodes pruned historic data ([#13570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/13570)).
*   **Transaction Pool Logic:** Work began on `op-reth/txpool` to reserve Isthmus operator fees during balance checks, ensuring parity with `op-geth` ([#21609](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21609)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Optimism Sepolia Intrinsic Gas Too High After Karst Hard Fork [#21457](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21457)
The issue, which caused `eth_estimateGas` to return "-32000 intrinsic gas too high" on OP Sepolia after the Karst hard fork, has been resolved. The fix was merged and released in `op-reth/v2.3.3`. The problem was observed across multiple RPC providers, and while `staticCall` succeeded and sending with an explicit `gasLimit` worked, `eth_estimateGas` failed.

### op-reth: update revm dependency to 2.4.0 / 2.3.1 [#21524](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21524)
This issue is a placeholder to update the `revm` dependency once a new release is available. The task is assigned to @joshklop, and the team is monitoring for the new release.

### Flaky test: `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` [#21635](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21635)
The `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` test is exhibiting flakiness in CI. The root cause has been identified: in follow-mode light sequencer runs, `FollowSource` could process an upstream local-safe head ahead of the current unsafe head, leading to stale queued build work. This stale build would then hit a "missing parent header" error, stopping the light sequencer. A draft PR ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21637](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21637)) has been created to address this by forcing a reset of active sequencers on upstream local-safe advance/divergence, clearing stale build states, and dropping stale queued build-start events.

### Re-enable or retire fuzzing [#21636](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-analytics/issues/21636)
An audit of all Go fuzz tests in the repository was conducted. The audit revealed that the current time-bounded exploration (`go test -fuzz ... -fuzztime 10–60s`) in CI jobs has limited value because there is no committed corpus, seeds are sparse, and deterministic value is already covered by regular unit tests. The recommendation is to retire all six PR-time fuzzing jobs as they offer minimal benefit beyond the existing seed subtests and incur CI costs and maintenance overhead. The fuzz functions themselves will be kept as they continue to run as deterministic seed tests in normal unit test jobs. A separate ticket might be opened for a more effective nightly fuzzing job, but only if it includes a committed seed corpus, meaningful fuzz time, and crash-artifact persistence. The issue is being closed via PR #21639.

- **`opgeth-decoupling`: make `op-service/sources` the OP-aware eth client** [#20264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20264)
  Discussion on the `op-batcher` migration strategy has evolved. It was determined that `op-batcher` cannot migrate to `InfoAndUserTxs` and will instead go payload-native. This is because `InfoAndUserTxs` drops necessary L1-info deposit transactions and post-execution transactions required for batch building. The batcher will now fetch `*eth.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` via `PayloadByNumber`. The partitioned accessors (`InfoAndUserTxs`, `InfoAndDeposits`, `InfoAndFirstDeposit`) will still be added for test migrations. Critical considerations for receipt root derivation and transaction hash derivation were also highlighted.

- **`opgeth-decoupling`: swap call-sites to `op-core/*` across `op-node`, `op-service`, `op-batcher`** [#20263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20263)
  All three sub-issues related to this task are now closed. The remaining scope of this issue is being tracked in [#21901](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21901), which covers `PostExecTx` span-batch swap and one-off fork symbols. The issue will close once [#21901](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21901) is landed.

- **Flake: `reth-optimism-node` integration test `peers_negotiate_eth_69` SIGSEGVs on teardown** [#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20973)
  An independent review of this flake was conducted, and a candidate upstream fix was evaluated. The "detached payload thread polls a torn-down runtime" mechanism, previously suspected, was refuted by experiments. The actual mechanism of the segfault remains unidentified. The "own-runtime" patch is not being pursued as a fix because its causal claim is contradicted by experiments. The review highlighted that `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` does not affect SIGSEGVs, and local reproduction attempts are likely futile. The recommended next step is to capture a core dump/faulting stack in CI to identify the root cause. A different approach is being explored in [#21562](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/21562).

- **Flaky test: `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`** [#21635](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21635)
  The root cause of this recurring flake has been identified. `FollowSource` could canonicalize upstream block N+1 while the light sequencer had a timer armed against N, leading to a build start on a removed parent. This resulted in `missing parent header` and `Invalid payload attributes`, causing a critical shutdown. A draft PR ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#21913](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21913)) has been created to fix this by rejecting non-derived build starts unless their parent block ID matches the engine controller's current unsafe block ID. Verification shows the fix is effective, with regressions passing consistently.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### op-geth Decoupling: L2 Transaction Representation and Client Updates
Discussions on [#20264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20264) (opgeth-decoupling: make op-service/sources the OP-aware eth client) revealed a design correction for the `op-batcher` migration. It was determined that `op-batcher` cannot migrate to `InfoAndUserTxs` and will instead use `PayloadByNumber` to fetch `*eth.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope`. This is because `InfoAndUserTxs` drops critical information required for batch building, such as the L1-info deposit transaction and post-exec transactions. The partitioned accessors (`InfoAndUserTxs`, `InfoAndDeposits`, `InfoAndFirstDeposit`) will still be added for test migrations. Further complexities were noted regarding `optypes.Receipts` root derivation, which requires handling three distinct OP arms (post-Canyon deposit receipts, pre-Canyon deposit receipts, and `0x7D` post-exec receipts), and `FetchReceipts` needing to derive transaction hashes from raw transactions.

### op-geth Decoupling: Call-site Swaps and Transition Scaffolding
Regarding [#20263](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20263) (opgeth-decoupling: swap call-sites to op-core/* across op-node, op-service, op-batcher), it was noted that all three sub-issues are closed, and the remaining scope is tracked in [#21901](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21901). A key point from earlier discussions highlighted that `optypes` helpers like `IsDepositTx(tx)` are transition scaffolding, operating on `*types.Transaction` from op-geth. These helpers are temporary and will be removed at the final cutover, serving to decouple call sites from op-geth internals before the L2 transaction representation changes. Developers are advised to prefer decoding to `optypes.DepositTx` directly when possible, rather than building new long-lived APIs on these temporary helpers.

### Flaky Test: reth-optimism-node integration test SIGSEGV
The ongoing investigation into [#20973](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20973) (flake: reth-optimism-node integration test peers_negotiate_eth_69 SIGSEGVs on teardown) received a detailed update. An independent review refuted the earlier hypothesis that the segfault was caused by a detached payload thread polling a torn-down runtime. Experimental verification showed that the `select(on_shutdown, task)` wrapper prevents polling a dead runtime, and `payload-builder` threads are gone before `exit_group`. The "own-runtime patch" is not being pursued as a fix because it doesn't change behavior at runtime death. The actual mechanism of the segfault remains unidentified, but potential culprits include `mdbx_env_close_ex` not being called, detached `engine` and `persistence` threads, or RocksDB background threads racing with C++ static destructors. The recommended next step is to capture a core dump/faulting stack in CI to pinpoint the exact cause.

### Flaky Test: TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement
For [#21635](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21635) (flaky test: `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`), a root cause and fix update were provided. The flake is caused by `FollowSource` canonicalizing upstream block N+1 while the light sequencer still has a timer armed against block N. This can lead to the timer running first and emitting a build start on the removed parent N, causing `missing parent header` and `Invalid payload attributes` errors in op-reth, leading to a critical shutdown. The flakiness stems from the Go `select` ordering. The proposed fix involves rejecting non-derived build starts unless their parent block ID matches the engine controller's current unsafe block ID, with the check and follow-source sharing the controller mutex to prevent stale Engine API calls. Verification with focused regressions showed the fix to be effective.

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Flaky Test Resolution
The long-standing flaky test `TestExecutePayloadSuccess` ([#19898](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19898)) was closed today. The issue was identified as a race condition where the `debug_executePayload` RPC on `op-reth` queried the proofs ExEx store before it had indexed the block. The fix involved waiting for the proofs ExEx store to be ready for the target block, specifically by waiting for the later of the two transaction receipt blocks before fetching account proofs.
